fields.hero_h1: Window Crank Repair in Toronto and the GTA
fields.hero_subhead: Stripped crank, broken operator, or a casement that will not close? We repair the hardware, not the whole window, across the GTA.
fields.overview_body:
When a casement or awning window will not open, close, or seal, the glass is usually fine, the hardware has worn out. SolidGuard does window crank repair across Toronto and the GTA: stripped crank handles, broken operators, and seized hinges. A quick window hardware repair restores the window for a fraction of the cost of replacing it.

We carry common operators and parts for most makes, so casement window repair and window hinge repair are often done in a single visit. Cranks, operators, hinges, and locks, we match the part and set the window so it closes tight again.
fields.repairfirst_body: A window that will not crank rarely needs replacing. The operator or hinge is the worn part, and that is what we fix.

whatwehandle_items.item: Loose or failed locks and latches
Windows that will not seal shut

faqs.question: My window crank spins but the window will not move. Can you fix it?
faqs.answer: Yes. That is usually a stripped operator gear. A window crank repair replaces the operator and the window works again.

faqs.question: Do you repair casement and awning windows?
faqs.answer: Yes. Casement window repair and awning hardware are our common jobs, including operators, hinges, and locks.

faqs.question: Do I need a whole new window?
faqs.answer: Almost never. The glass is fine, the hardware is worn. A window hardware repair is far cheaper than replacement.

faqs.question: How fast can you come out?
faqs.answer: Same or next day across most of the GTA.
